name: cheque-verification-layoutllm
description: End-to-end computer vision + NLP system for automated bank cheque verification — LayoutLMv3 encoder fused with a LoRA fine-tuned TinyLlama decoder to extract payee, amounts, date & signature as structured JSON, with automated fraud checks and a Streamlit demo.

paragraphs: A hybrid vision-language model that reads a photo of a bank cheque and turns it into structured, verifiable data.

Manual cheque processing is slow and error-prone: a clerk has to read handwriting, cross-check the amount in words against the amount in digits, confirm a signature is present, and do it all correctly, every time. This project builds an end-to-end computer vision + NLP pipeline that automates that job — it takes a photo of a bank cheque and outputs structured JSON (payee, date, numeric amount, amount in words, signature status) that a downstream fraud-check layer can validate automatically.
The core of the system is LayoutLLM, a "Frankenstein" architecture that fuses two pretrained models that were never designed to talk to each other:
features: LayoutLMv3 (the "eyes") — reads the cheque image and its 2D layout
TinyLlama-1.1B (the "brain") — generates the structured JSON output, fine-tuned with LoRA so only 0.2% of its parameters are ever updated

🧠 Custom multimodal architecture — a vision-layout encoder (LayoutLMv3) bolted onto a generative language decoder (TinyLlama) via a trainable linear projector, trained end-to-end for structured extraction rather than…

⚡ Parameter-efficient fine-tuning — LoRA adapters on the decoder's attention projections mean only 2.25M of 1.1B parameters are trainable, making fine-tuning feasible on a single free-tier Colab/Kaggle GPU.

🧾 5,000-image synthetic cheque dataset, procedurally generated across 3 Pakistani bank templates (HBL, MCB, Meezan Bank) with randomized payees, amounts, dates, and signature presence — plus normalized bounding-box…
